title: Piezoelectronic access switch with pressure-driven insulator-metal channel
idea: Effect: pressure-induced insulator-to-metal transition. A thin AlScN piezo actuator driven by the wordline squeezes a ~5 nm SmSe-class valence-change piezoresistor in series with the storage node; at ~1 GPa it turns metallic, and when unpressed it is a ~0.5 eV-gap insulator, so the hold path is a true insulator rather than a subthreshold channel.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): off-current set by a band gap, not the 60 mV/dec subthreshold slope; claims >100x lower leakage, refresh interval from 64 ms to seconds, and refresh's 16-33% idle power falls to ~1%.

title: Gate-triggered Mott-gap channel gives access device without subthreshold tail
idea: Effect: filling-controlled Mott transition. The access channel is a correlated oxide (e.g., electron-doped SmNiO3 or Ca2RuO4) where the wordline field adds ~0.1 carrier per site and collapses the Mott gap abruptly; below critical filling it is a gapped insulator whose leakage scales as exp(-Eg/kT) instead of following a gradual subthreshold slope.
why: Leakage tail and voltage floor (facts 3, 10): an abrupt switch allows wordline swing ~1.5 V instead of 3 V (~4x less wordline CV2) while holding <1 aA, removing most refresh.

title: Resonant-tunneling access diode opens only at wordline-tuned resonance
idea: Effect: double-barrier resonant tunneling. Replace the access transistor with a vertical AlN/GaN/AlN (or SiO2/Si-well/SiO2) stack whose quantized well level aligns with the storage-node Fermi level only when the wordline, acting as a gate on the well, pulls it into resonance; off-resonance transmission is 10^6-10^9 lower and fixed by barrier thickness rather than doping.
why: 3D blocker (fact 2): a thin vertical film stack replaces the lateral transistor, so tiers stack without lithography of channels; leakage decoupled from channel length (fact 4).

title: Spin-Hall-rotated half-metal spin valve as channel-free access gate
idea: Effect: spin Hall torque plus half-metallic spin filtering. Each cell's access element is a Co2MnSi/MgO/Co2MnSi junction; a current pulse in a BiSb topological-insulator wordline strip (no tungsten) exerts spin-orbit torque that rotates the row's free layers parallel (conducting) during access and antiparallel (no minority states at EF, blocking) during hold.
why: Leakage and wordline voltage (facts 3, 10): off-state set by spin polarization not temperature; row select by ~0.1 V current pulses instead of 3 V swings; 10-100x lower leakage if polarization >0.99.

title: Optical wordlines open dark-insulating photoconductive access pillars
idea: Effect: photoconductivity. Each storage capacitor reaches the bitline through a wide-gap photoconductor pillar (amorphous Se or ZnS, dark resistivity >10^13 ohm-cm, engineered short carrier lifetime for <10 ns turn-off); a row is opened by light from an on-die SiN waveguide grating, so the wordline is photons and the hold state is a dark insulator.
why: Leakage tail and periphery (facts 3, 7): attoamp dark current makes refresh near-zero; removes wordline drivers, row charge pumps and VPP from the ~49% periphery.

title: Magnetostrictive NEMS relay access with vacuum-gap off state
idea: Effect: magnetostriction. A Galfenol (FeGa) nanobeam above each storage contact elongates in the field of a current-carrying wordline and touches a Ru contact pad; with no current a ~5 nm sealed vacuum gap separates node and bitline, giving zero channel leakage; GHz mechanical resonance at 10 nm scale keeps actuation in ns.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ideal mechanical off state leaves only capacitor-dielectric leakage, retention minutes to hours; actuation is by current, avoiding the 3 V gate swing (fact 10). Risk: contact wear at 1e15 cycles.

title: Vacuum-nanogap field-emission access device with gated emitter pair
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim field emission into vacuum. A sealed 10 nm vacuum gap sits between the bitline contact and the storage node with sharp emitter tips on both sides (for both write polarities) and a ring wordline gate around the gap; the gate raises tip fields above ~3 V/nm only during access, while at rest a ~4 eV work-function barrier conducts nothing measurable.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): no semiconductor channel means no GIDL, junction or trap-assisted tails; retention bounded by capacitor dielectric; radiation-hard bonus.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO gate stack buys 0.3 V higher access Vt
idea: Effect: ferroelectric negative capacitance. Insert a 3-4 nm HZO layer capacitance-matched to the buried-channel access transistor's gate oxide so the stack amplifies surface potential and swings below 60 mV/dec in the switching window; raise Vt ~0.3 V (up to ~5 decades less subthreshold current) while keeping on-current at equal or lower wordline voltage.
why: Leakage tail and voltage floor (facts 3, 10): 10-100x retention, or wordline from 3 V to ~2.2 V (~45% less wordline CV2).

title: Bank-wide ferroelectric back gate flips array Vt for sleep
idea: Effect: remanent ferroelectric polarization. A shared HZO back gate under each subarray's vertical-channel transistors is pulsed once on self-refresh entry to polarization 'down', adding ~0.4 V of nonvolatile back-bias that shuts the leakage tail with no continuous negative pump; on exit a pulse restores 'up' for full drive.
why: Idle refresh power (fact 3): self-refresh interval x10-30 with zero standby bias power; removes negative-bias pump area from periphery (fact 7).

title: Field-ionized deep-dopant extensions stay semi-insulating while holding
idea: Effect: Poole-Frenkel field-assisted ionization. Dope the storage-node-side extension with a deep donor (e.g., S or Se in Si, ~0.3 eV, kept away from midgap to avoid SRH generation) so it is mostly un-ionized and semi-insulating at the low hold field, but the wordline-on field lowers the barrier and ionizes it within picoseconds so the extension conducts.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): removes the field-enhanced junction path that dominates the <=13 fA tail; claims ~10x tail reduction. Risk: deep levels as generation centres.

title: Hydrogen-terminated diamond access channel using surface transfer doping
idea: Effect: surface transfer doping. A bonded thin diamond film with an H-terminated surface and MoO3 acceptor cap forms a 2D hole gas that the wordline depletes; the 5.5 eV bulk band gap makes thermal generation essentially nil, and diamond's ~2000 W/mK conductivity spreads array heat.
why: Leakage tail and thermal (fact 3): retention hours and no high-temperature refresh doubling; bonded diamond layers are a route to cool 3D tiers (fact 2).

title: Graphene-silicon barristor access with gate-tuned Schottky barrier height
idea: Effect: thermionic emission over a gate-tunable Schottky barrier. The storage node contacts silicon through a graphene electrode whose low density of states lets the wordline shift its work function ~0.5 eV: barrier ~0.9 eV in hold (thermionic current ~aA), ~0.4 eV during access.
why: Leakage and 3D (facts 2, 3, 4): leakage set by barrier height exponentially, not by a 12 nm channel's slope; vertical junction is litho-light and stackable.

title: Pyroelectric wordline layer auto-cancels hot-die leakage rise
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. A poled AlScN film in the access gate stack generates bound charge equivalent to a more negative gate bias as temperature rises (~-2 to -4 mV/K), offsetting the access transistor's Vt drop that doubles leakage every ~10 C.
why: Refresh bandwidth (fact 3): flattens retention vs temperature so >85 C operation needs no 2x refresh (10-20% bandwidth); passive, zero power. Risk: pyro charge screening over long times.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods run DRAM at 77 K, refresh off
idea: Effect: Arrhenius freeze-out of generation and subthreshold leakage. DIMMs/HBM sit on closed-loop LN2 cold plates; at 77 K subthreshold slope is ~15-20 mV/dec and generation ~exp(-Eg/2kT) collapses, so retention exceeds hours, refresh is disabled and Vt/VDD are retuned for cold operation.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth to ~0 (fact 3), wire resistance ~6x lower (fact 5), lower VDD (fact 10); cooling cost amortized at rack scale.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode pair self-restores each bit without refresh
idea: Effect: interband tunneling negative differential resistance. Two nanoscale p++/n++ Ge (or SiGe) Esaki diodes stacked in series on the storage node form a Goto pair; a pA standby current biases them so the node has two stable voltages that actively restore against leakage, giving a refresh-free 1T2D cell barely larger than 1T1C.
why: Refresh eliminated (fact 3) at near-DRAM density; trade-off is pA/cell standby current, which must beat 46 fJ/bit refresh.

title: Diffusive silver-filament selector blocks access transistor subthreshold leakage
idea: Effect: electrochemical ion migration with spontaneous filament dissolution. A 3 nm SiOxNy:Ag layer in the storage-node contact forms a filament within ns when the open access transistor applies 0.5-1 V across it, then self-dissolves within ~1 us after the wordline closes, leaving an insulating gap (<1 aA) in series with the transistor's leakage tail.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): series ion gap claims 100x retention. Risk: 1e15 endurance and post-write dissolution window.

title: Package magnet quenches spin-dependent trap-assisted leakage in VRT cells
idea: Effect: spin-dependent recombination/hopping. Trap-assisted tunneling via paramagnetic defect pairs needs spin-pair conversion; a ~0.3-1 T ferrite or SmCo magnet in the package lid polarizes defect and carrier spins, slowing the hop rate of the dominant variable-retention-time trap pairs.
why: Targets the VRT component of the leakage tail (fact 3); honest gain unknown (known effects 0.1-10%), large only if a giant-effect defect class exists; zero die change.

title: Phononic wordlines address rows by acoustic resonance frequency
idea: Effect: piezotronic strain from resonant surface acoustic waves. Each row's access junction sits on a phononic resonator tuned to a unique GHz frequency (512 rows over 1-5 GHz at Q~1000); refresh broadcasts a frequency sequence from one interdigitated transducer and only the resonating row gets enough strain to open, replacing decoded wordline drivers.
why: Periphery and refresh energy (facts 7, 3, 10): row decoders and 3 V wordline drivers leave the refresh path; claims ~10x lower refresh selection energy.

title: Maxwell-Wagner bilayer capacitor back-fills leaked charge from interface reservoir
idea: Effect: interfacial (Maxwell-Wagner-Sillars) polarization, i.e., dielectric absorption. The cell capacitor is a high-k/low-conductivity bilayer engineered so interface charge accumulates over ms after a write and re-emerges as the node droops, like a capacitor's recovery voltage; a reset pulse on writes clears ghost charge from the previous value.
why: Retention x2-5 without a better transistor (fact 3). Risk: data-history ghosting and slow charging.

title: 1.5 nm quantum-confined silicon access sheet widens effective band gap
idea: Effect: quantum confinement. Thin the vertical access channel to ~1.5 nm Si so subband confinement raises the effective gap from 1.12 to ~1.6-1.8 eV, cutting band-to-band GIDL and SRH generation (proportional to ni ~ exp(-Eg/2kT)) by up to ~10^4 at the storage junction.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 10-100x retention, compatible with 4F2 vertical-channel cells. Risk: Vt variation ~1/t^2 and mobility loss.

title: Lifetime-matched no-refresh regions hold short-lived AI tensors
idea: Effect: exponential RC charge decay used as a free timer. A new mode register and allocator hint expose per-bank refresh-off regions; the runtime places activations, KV-cache scratch and gradient buffers that live <32 ms there (each write restores charge), so those rows are never refreshed.
why: Refresh bandwidth and energy (fact 3): with 50-80% of accelerator DRAM traffic short-lived, removes refresh for those regions (10-20% bandwidth at 32-64 Gb); needs controller/OS changes.

title: Dopant-free charge-plasma access transistor removes implant-driven leakage outliers
idea: Effect: work-function-induced charge plasma. Source/drain are induced electrostatically in an undoped channel by low-work-function (Hf-based) contacts, so there is no implanted metallurgical junction: no implant damage, no end-of-range defects and no random-dopant clusters that create the 13 fA outliers.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): narrows the retention distribution so refresh is set near the median, not the 1-ppm cell; claims 4-8x less refresh.

title: Crested tunnel barrier serves as two-terminal field-switched access
idea: Effect: field-sensitive tunneling through a crested (peaked) barrier. A Si3N4/AlN/Si3N4-type trilayer replaces the access channel; high bias pulls the central peak down (current rises ~10^12 over a 3x voltage change) so the node writes in ns at +/-3 V but leaks <1 aA at the +/-0.5 V hold and half-select bias.
why: 3D and leakage (facts 2, 3): two-terminal vertical stack layers into tiers without a lateral transistor; claims >=10 s retention. Risk: barrier wear and disturb.

title: Wordline-gated Coulomb-blockade nanodot valve in storage-node contact
idea: Effect: Coulomb blockade. A ~1 nm Pt or Si nanodot between two tunnel barriers sits in the storage-node plug, capacitively gated by the same wordline: wordline-high moves the dot to its charge-degeneracy point (conducts), wordline-low leaves it deep in blockade with charging energy ~0.6 eV, above the 0.5 V node-to-bitline hold bias, so it blocks transistor leakage in series. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): claims 10x retention used for die-internal refresh skipping behind standard REF. Risk: on-current through dots vs tRCD/tWR (needs parallel dots).

title: Buried piezoresistive stressor trades extra mobility for higher access Vt
idea: Effect: piezoresistance (strain-shifted conduction valleys). Wrap the buried-channel access transistor with a ~1.5 GPa tensile SiN or AlN liner, raising electron mobility 30-50%, then spend that drive on ~90 mV higher Vt, so write speed and VPP stay the same. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ~1.5 decades less subthreshold leakage; die refreshes each row only every 2nd-4th REF internally.

title: Resonant LC wordline driver recycles refresh switching energy
idea: Effect: LC resonance and adiabatic charging. During internal refresh bursts, wordlines swing through an interposer or RDL spiral inductor resonating with the wordline capacitance, returning charge to the tank instead of dumping it to ground; the burst still fits inside today's tRFC. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Voltage floor and refresh energy (facts 3, 10): recovers 50-70% of 3 V wordline CV2, cutting refresh energy ~25-40%.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal hardens traps behind the leakage tail
idea: Effect: kinetic isotope effect. Replace the final forming-gas anneal with 10-20 atm D2 so Si-D bonds passivate interface and GIDL-region traps; Si-D resists field- and hot-carrier-driven depassivation ~10-50x better than Si-H, so fewer traps reactivate into weak or VRT cells over life. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ~2x longer guaranteed internal refresh period; deuterium from heavy water is not a chokepoint.

title: Field-drifted mobile-ion Vt trim repairs weak cells at sort
idea: Effect: thermally activated ion migration. A sub-nm Cs-doped sublayer sits in the access gate dielectric; at wafer sort the tester biases only retention-failing rows at ~200 C so ions drift from the channel side to the gate side, raising those transistors' Vt ~0.1-0.2 V; high activation energy (~1.5 eV) freezes them for life at operating temperature. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ppm weak rows join the bulk distribution, so internal refresh can follow the median; claims 4x refresh interval.

title: Photon-emission retention mapping fuses per-row internal refresh bins
idea: Effect: junction and hot-carrier electroluminescence. At sort the array is biased to stress leakage paths and a cooled InGaAs camera images the faint NIR emission; leaky row segments glow, so a weak-row map is captured in seconds instead of hours of retention testing and burned into fuses; the die then refreshes strong rows only every 4th REF. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3): -50-75%; optics resolve row segments, not single cells, which is enough for row binning.

title: Power-up microheater pulses anneal variable-retention-time defects
idea: Effect: thermally activated defect reconfiguration. VRT cells toggle as a metastable defect switches configuration; TiN microheaters in thermally isolated mats deliver ~us pulses at ~250 C during the JEDEC initialization window (before data exists), biased with a gate field that favours the low-leakage configuration, pruning the VRT population each boot. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): fewer VRT escapes lets the die relax internal refresh ~2x. Risk: which defect state annealing favours is unproven.

title: Thin-film Peltier layer in HBM base die cools the array
idea: Effect: Peltier thermoelectric cooling. Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 superlattice pads between the base logic die and the lowest DRAM die, plus over hotspot columns, pump heat to the lid only when the stack exceeds ~80 C, holding array temperature ~10 C lower (retention roughly doubles per 10 C). DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Refresh bandwidth (fact 3): avoids the 2x refresh regime above 85 C (10-20% bandwidth); costs some pump power.

title: Low-melt alloy latent-heat pockets in HBM dummy-bump cavities
idea: Effect: latent heat of fusion. Sealed dummy-bump and dummy-TSV cavities are filled with a 60-70 C Bi-In-Sn eutectic that melts during compute bursts, clamping DRAM die temperature below the 85 C refresh-doubling threshold for tens of seconds and refreezing in idle. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Refresh bandwidth (fact 3): keeps refresh at 1x during bursts (+10-20% peak bandwidth) with no power draw.

title: Interface dipole sets access Vt so channel doping can drop
idea: Effect: interfacial dipole at the high-k/SiO2 boundary. An Al2O3 dipole monolayer shifts the buried-wordline gate's effective work function by +0.2-0.3 V, letting channel boron doping fall ~3x; lower doping lowers the peak storage-junction field, and field-enhanced trap-assisted tunneling drops ~10x. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ~3-4x internal refresh relaxation from a single film change.

title: Lattice-matched GaP storage-node contact blocks band-to-band tunneling
idea: Effect: heterojunction band offset. A few-nm epitaxial GaP layer (0.4% lattice mismatch to Si, Eg 2.26 eV) at the gate-overlapped storage-node contact forces GIDL tunneling across a wider gap (rate ~exp(-Eg^1.5/F)), cutting GIDL by up to ~10^3. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): GIDL dominates at negative wordline hold bias; claims 4x internal refresh skip. Risk: Ga cross-contamination in a DRAM line.

title: Positive fixed-charge nitride spacer relieves storage-junction GIDL field
idea: Effect: field-effect passivation by fixed dielectric charge (the solar-cell passivation trick). A SiNx spacer holding ~+2e12 cm^-2 fixed charge lines only the gate-to-storage-node overlap, accumulating electrons at the n+ surface so band bending under a low wordline is reduced and GIDL falls. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ~10x less GIDL in hold; zero added masks if the spacer deposition is swapped.

title: On-die telegraph-noise detector catches VRT cells in the field
idea: Effect: random telegraph noise from single-trap capture and emission. Inside idle REF windows each bank re-reads sample rows with a deliberately lowered sense reference; cells whose margin toggles (RTN signature) are logged in an on-die CAM and get extra internal refreshes while all other rows get fewer. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): catches cells that pass factory test then turn leaky, enabling safe 2-4x internal refresh relaxation.

title: Antiferroelectric capacitor pins stored-one voltage as charge reservoir
idea: Effect: antiferroelectric double-hysteresis switching. The cell capacitor uses AFE ZrO2 with plate bias set so a stored '1' sits just above the backward switching field; as leakage drains charge, polarization release (~2Pr x area, ~10x the linear charge) holds the node near that voltage, which stays above the sense threshold, and reads look like normal charge sharing. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Capacitor charge wall and leakage (facts 1, 3): effective storage charge ~10x, retention ~5-10x. Risk: AFE endurance toward 1e15 cycles.

title: Molybdenum buried wordlines exploit shorter electron mean free path
idea: Effect: electron mean-free-path size effect (Fuchs-Sondheimer/Mayadas-Shatzkes). Replace TiN/W buried wordlines with barrierless Mo or Ru (mean free path ~11 and ~7 nm vs ~19 nm for W), cutting 10 nm-line resistance ~30-40% and freeing the barrier's trench volume; faster wordline edges shorten each internal refresh burst. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Refresh time and resources (facts 3, resources): ~2x lower wordline RC, ~20-30% shorter refresh activity, and tungsten (China ~80%) removed from the array.

title: Nanosecond laser melt regrows defect-free storage junctions
idea: Effect: liquid-phase epitaxial regrowth. After the storage-node implant, a ~50 ns UV/green laser pulse melts only the top ~20 nm, regrowing the junction epitaxially and dissolving end-of-range dislocation loops that act as generation centres, while the short thermal budget spares buried wordlines. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 2-3x tail compression, translated into internal refresh relaxation.

title: Carbon-cluster proximity gettering borrowed from image-sensor dark current
idea: Effect: impurity gettering. C3H5 molecular-ion clusters implanted ~1 um below the array (the CMOS image-sensor technique that cut dark current) form a dense sink that traps Fe, Cu and Ni during thermal steps, pulling midgap metal generation centres away from storage junctions. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 2-5x lower junction leakage tail, the same physics as CIS dark current; one substrate step.

title: Arrhenius canary rows set the die's internal refresh skipping
idea: Effect: thermally activated leakage with known activation energy (~0.6 eV). Each mat holds canary rows with deliberately smaller capacitors that fail at a known fraction of real-cell retention; counters time their decay at actual temperature, and the die skips REF work on real rows whenever canaries prove margin. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Refresh energy and busy time (fact 3): turns the worst-case 32/64 ms guard band into measured margin, -50-80% refresh work at typical temperature.

title: Voltage-stacked subarray pairs halve refresh supply current
idea: Effect: series voltage stacking (charge conservation). Two subarrays refreshed together run in stacked domains, A between VDD and VDD/2 and B between VDD/2 and 0 with plates biased per domain, so the restore current drawn through A's sense amps is reused by B instead of returning to ground. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Refresh energy (fact 3): ~2x less supply charge per refreshed bit pair, with no external voltage change.

title: Majority-state inversion plus bitline parking silences idle leakage
idea: Effect: asymmetric leakage (a node at substrate and bitline potential cannot decay). On write, each row gets an internal inversion flag in on-die ECC spare bits chosen so most cells hold the low state; in self-refresh/power-down the bitlines park at 0 V, so those cells see zero drain bias and zero junction bias, and bitlines re-equalize within tXS. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): halves or better the leak-exposed cells per row; with on-die ECC, claims 1.5-2x longer self-refresh interval.

title: Charge-transfer pre-sensing resolves half-decayed cells within tRCD
idea: Effect: charge transfer through a subthreshold-biased MOSFET (CCD floating-diffusion style). A charge-transfer preamplifier between bitline and sense amp funnels bitline charge onto a small sense node, multiplying signal ~5-10x by C_BL/C_sense, so cells that have lost ~70% of their charge still resolve. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Retention criterion (facts 1, 3): time-to-fail lengthens 2-3x for the same leakage, so internal refresh halves.

title: Air gaps between buried wordlines stop passing-gate leakage
idea: Effect: fringing-field coupling (passing-gate effect). The oxide between neighbouring buried wordlines and the storage-node junction becomes a sealed air gap (k~1), so a neighbour's 3 V swing no longer lowers the barrier of the passing cell, removing the activity-dependent leakage spikes that force conservative refresh. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) with row-hammer relief (fact 9): claims ~2x tail improvement; process drop-in.

title: Capacitive-bootstrap wordline drivers retire the global VPP pump
idea: Effect: capacitive bootstrapping. Each wordline driver self-boosts: its gate node floats as the wordline rises and a coupling capacitor kicks it to ~2.8 V, so VPP is created locally from the transition rather than by a 30-40%-efficient global charge pump; timing fits normal ACT and REF. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Voltage floor and periphery (facts 10, 7): refresh energy -20-30% and pump area freed.
